sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Aztekium ritteri is a very small, slow-growing cactus native to dry parts of northeastern Mexico. It has a grey-green, nearly spineless body with narrow ribs and produces pink flowers. Annual growth can be only about 1–2 mm; published accounts differ on the precise limits of its range.

sections.title: Food and image
sections.text: No edible use was verified. The plate's small ribbed body, sparse spines and pink flowers match the plant; it should not be mistaken for a mature, fast-growing garden cactus.

sections.title: Related cacti
sections.text: The closely related genus Astrophytum includes A. caput-medusae and A. ornatum, which have markedly different body shapes and faster visible growth.
